reasons: Section 2.1 as drafted is a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with express 'without reduction or termination rights' — squarely the rule's walk-away position and a clear failure of the fallback (12-month, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty), so 'deviation' is the correct classification and not over-flagging of an acceptable fallback.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it removes the take-or-pay and substitutes payment for Services used or ordered, matching the preferred position and consistent with Section 7.1's per-Order-Form fee construct and Section 12.3's acknowledgement of no minimum-volume commitment.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.951 changed-character ratio) is expected here — the rule's redline guidance is to delete or narrow the commitment, and the clause is a single sentence whose entire operative content is the offending obligation, so a whole-clause replacement is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

The comment is accurate, in the required tone and prefix, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and the Section 12.3 inconsistency, and offers the 12-month reducible/true-up fallback without lecturing.
